prerequisites: Electrical circuits (basic electrical bipoles, Kirchhoff’s laws of voltage and current, analysis of dc and ac systems, three-phase systems, concepts of active power, reactive power and power factor)

Basic concepts related to electrical machines (structure, operating principles and basic models of dc machines, permanent magnet synchronous machines and asynchronous machines) from the course "Electrical circuits and machines"
Math: basics of differential calculus and trigonometric formulas
Physics: basics of mechanics and electromagnetism
Basics of automatic control: concepts of transfer function and frequency response and drawing of Bode diagrams

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the operating principles and fields of operation of the main electrical machines and drives.
Master terminology and parameters characterizing electric drives.
Design simple current and speed controllers for dc and ac drives.
Read and correctly interpret nameplate data of the considered electrical machines and drives.
Understand the main applications of electric drives for the transition of our modern society towards more sustainable energy paradigms.

syllabus_topics: Power electronic converters for electric drives: Power switching devices
DC-DC converters operating in 1, 2 and 4 quadrants
Voltage source three phase inverters and main modulation techniques
Dc motor: review of the dc motor: structure, operating principle and dynamical model
Drives for dc machines (current and speed loops)
Exercises on dc motors and drives
Stationary and synchronous reference frames: space vectors: definition, properties, and examples
Permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM): review of the PMSM
Dynamical model in a rotating reference frame synchronous with the rotor
Discussion and comparison of different types of controllers
Exercises and examples on permanent magnets motors and drives
Asynchronous machine: review of the asynchronous motors
Overview of the main types of drives for asynchronous machines
Scalar control of the speed (V/Hz control)
Exercises on asynchronous motors and drives
Reluctance machines and stepper motors: types
Electrification process of the modern society and examples of application of electric drives

assessment_methods.method: Final written test (theoretical content and exercises)

assessment_rules: To pass the exam, students must pass a final written test. The written test can include both open questions and multiple-choice questions. A maximum score of 31 points can be earned. If the student earns at least 18/30 points, the exam is passed; otherwise, it must be repeated in a later session.
